subject: Post-demo: RAG qualification runbook & next steps

Subject: Post-demo: RAG qualification runbook & next steps

Hi María —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side plus a proposed lightweight runbook to qualify RAG fit for Cascade Health. Goal: give you concrete benchmarks and a repeatable probe that shows grounding quality, latency, and cost tradeoffs on your typical clinical-query traffic.

Recap (30-min demo)
- Use case: clinician-facing search + short summarization for charting and CDS — high priority on grounding/PII controls.
- Data: ~9M doc fragments in production (structured + unstructured notes); primary vectors in your existing Milvus cluster.
- SLOs you called out: 95th pct latency < 1.2s for 1k qps burst; grounding precision @1 target > 92% for high-confidence answers.

Recommended next steps (runbook draft)
1) Sample dataset: you upload a 5k redacted query set + 2k representative docs to an S3 bucket we can access (we’ll provide a presigned). We prefer realistic queries (clinician phrasing + typos). Template attached: cascade_rag_probe_template.csv.

2) Probe config (short smoke):
   - Retriever: dense vector (contrastive embedding) with a hybrid fallback to BM25 for sparse matches.
   - Embedding model: run experiments with Redwood-embed-compact-v1 and open-embedding-2 as a baseline.
   - Top-K: retrieve top_k=100, rerank top_n=5 (see Ben’s technical note below for why).
   - Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for top precision (fine-tune on your relevance labels if available). If latency budget is tight, consider a bi-encoder + lightweight re-ranker cascade.

3) Model candidates for the generation step (we’ll benchmark each):
   - Redwood-chat-13B-quant (fast, good grounding when primed)
   - Orca-Medium-8B (cost-efficient baseline)
   - Llama2-chat-70B-8bit (higher quality/latency tradeoff)

4) Metrics & evaluation artifacts:
   - Grounding precision@1, hallucination rate (human-labeled sample of 500 queries), MRR, token cost per response, 95p latency.
   - We'll run automatic synthetic probes + human review on a 500-case judgment set.

5) Timeline (suggested):
   - Day 0: you upload probe CSV + sample docs.
   - Day 1–2: embedding + retrieval baseline runs.
   - Day 3–5: reranker + generator probes + internal QA.
   - Day 6: demo results + go/no-go.

Attachments: cascade_rag_probe_template.csv, redwood_rag_prompt_suite_v1.zip (prompt sets + eval instructions).

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm a target test window (next two weeks?) and who will own the sample upload on your side?
- Any constraints on PII handling or redaction we should follow beyond the HIPAA redaction note you mentioned?

Happy to run a technical kickoff with Ben and Jasmine tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Sofia

Hi all — jumping in with concrete defaults and why we recommend them. These are what we’ll use for the first probe; we can iterate after we see the initial numbers.

Retriever/embedding
- Embedding model: redwood-embed-compact-v1 (vector dim 768) as the default; run open-embedding-2 as a lower-cost baseline.
- Indexing: IVF-PQ for the 9M fragments (balanced recall/latency). If you prefer exact recall for the probe, we can run a smaller evaluation index with HNSW for the 5k-doc subset.
- Retrieval params: top_k=100 (dense) + BM25 fallback on no-match signals (empty vector or low-similarity). Pre-filter by doc_type for clinical notes vs admin docs to reduce noise.

Reranker & cascade
- Reranker type: cross-encoder (fine-tunable on human labels) for the high-precision path. Suggested hyperparams: batch_size=16, lr=2e-5, max_seq=512, train epochs=3 on ~1k labels.
- Operational cascade: bi-encoder for initial recall (fast), then cross-encoder rerank top 100 -> select top_n=5 for prompting. This keeps latency predictable while improving precision.

Generator model & prompt strategy
- Generator candidates we’ll benchmark: redwood-chat-13B-quant (default), llama2-chat-70b-8bit (high-quality baseline). Use retrieval-augmented prompts with an answer-verification step (explicit instruction to cite doc ids).
- Prompt set: short-answer + citation requirement, and a separate long-form summarization prompt. Included in redwood_rag_prompt_suite_v1.zip.

Benchmarks & instrumentation
- Metrics to capture: grounding_precision@1, hallucination_rate (human-verified), MRR@10, avg token cost, 95th latency. We’ll instrument token-level tracing so you can map cost to request types.
- Run plan: run a 1k-query automated sweep across model/re-ranker combinations, then human evaluate 500 queries for grounding precision.

Ops/Throughput notes
- Approx latency (estimates for planning, measured on Redwood Dedicated GPU pool):
   * redwood-chat-13B-quant + cross-encoder: median ~260ms (gen) + 120–250ms re-rank (depends on cross-encoder size) -> total p50 ~420–520ms.
   * llama2-chat-70b-8bit + cross-encoder: p50 ~900–1100ms.
- Token-cost estimates: full run numbers depend on prompt length; we’ll produce a small cost model during the probe.

I’ve attached reranker_config_v1.yaml and the probe CSV template for your upload. Happy to run the first sweep in a dedicated sandbox we provision for you.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sr ML Engineer, Model Ops
